newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta Drydocks workers hold demonstration.
newsitem.headline: Malta Drydocks workers hold demonstration.

text.p: Up to 3,200 workers at state-owned Malta Drydocks held a demonstration on Friday, calling for the resignation of the yard's chairman following a dispute over compensation for the heirs of nine workers killed two years ago.

Relatives of the workers, who died in an accidental explosion aboard the Libyan tanker Um El Faroud in February 1995, told dockyard council chairman Noel Zarb Adami on Tuesday they did not want compensation from the dockyard to be linked to any award for damages by the court.

Zarb Adami raised widespread indignation by walking out of the meeting, telling the relatives "see you in court in 10 years time," a reference to the length of time it takes for a case to be settled in a Maltese court.
Some 1,000 workers held a small demonstration at the dockyard on Thursday during their lunch break, expressing their solidarity with the victims.

But although by the evening they were told that compensation would be given as requested by the relatives, workers downed tools on Friday morning and held demonstrations in and around the dockyard, calling for Zarb Adami's resignation. The demonstrations continued in the afternoon.
Workers said they were insisting they should all be properly insured, but added that they were also blaming Zarb Adami for a drop in work orders at the cash-strapped yard.
Zarb Adami was appointed chairman in February after the government upset dockyard workers by removing the previous council, which was wholly elected by the workforce.
The measure was taken in an attempt to turn round fortunes at the dockyard, which has been making losses for the past few years.
